cards.explanation: The answer is Jesus Christ and God the Father. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says he was "…sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead…" (Galatians 1:1). He doesn't open with a résumé or a list of references, friends. He opens with the One who sent him.

The answer is True. Paul says he was sent by "…Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead…" (Galatians 1:1). Look who he points to first thing in the letter, friends. He's sent by the One who raised Jesus.
The answer is sins. Paul says Jesus "…gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age…" (Galatians 1:4). That's a rescue, friends. Jesus gave Himself for us.

The answer is False. Paul says Jesus gave Himself for our sins "…according to the will of our God and Father…" (Galatians 1:4). Not against it, according to it. And then Paul ends the thought with praise: "…to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen." (Galatians 1:5)

The answer is how quickly they're turning away. Paul writes, "I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ…" (Galatians 1:6). The word is quickly. I'd say that's Paul shaking his head at the speed of it.
The answer is a different gospel. Paul says they "…are turning to a different gospel…" (Galatians 1:6). Notice who they're deserting, too, friends: the One who called them by the grace of Christ.

The answer is False. Paul says this different gospel is "…not even a gospel." (Galatians 1:7). He doesn't call it a second flavor or a remix. Then he says that some people are troubling them and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.

The answer is distort. Paul says some people are "…troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ." (Galatians 1:7). Think of a stamp pressed crooked so the cookie comes out wrong. I know a thing or two about blurry stamps, believe me.

The answer is an angel from heaven. Paul says, "But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!" (Galatians 1:8). He includes himself and an angel from heaven. The message itself is what matters, friends, no matter who brings it.

The answer is Christ. Paul writes, "If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ." (Galatians 1:10). Right before that he asks, "Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God?" He knows whose servant he is.
